traceLoadsNone: Nothing in the design model reads this signal.
traceLoadsCompiledOnly: Only the compiled design has this signal, so its readers are not known.
traceLoadsLimits: Not listed: reads through hierarchical references from other instances.
traceLoadsOpaque: %@ statements slang could not elaborate may read it too.
traceLoadsInterfaceCapped: Interface reads past %@ instances are not listed.
traceXWhy_only: the only input with x or z
traceXWhy_earliest: the earliest x or z of %@ inputs
traceXWhy_same: the input with the same value
traceXWhy_heldLimited: held x since %@ or earlier (search limit)
traceXWhy_cause: the input that brought these x bits
traceXWhy_bits: the input the value's bits came from
traceXWhy_control: the condition that chose the statement (no data input)
traceXEnd_dumpStart: Stopped: %@ already has the x when the dump starts (its origin is before the dump).
traceXEnd_made: Root: this statement makes the value (no data input).
traceXEnd_noXInput: Root: this statement makes the x (no input has x or z).
traceXEnd_uninit: Root: never written since the start (uninitialised storage or a declaration).
traceXEnd_testbench: Root: the testbench sets the value.
traceXEnd_input: Root: an input of the top level.
traceXEnd_force: Root: a force or deposit from outside the instance.
traceXEnd_loop: Stopped: the x goes round a loop through %@.
traceXEnd_failed: Stopped: a step could not be traced.
traceXEnd_reloaded: Stopped: the waveform was reloaded during the trace. Trace again on the reloaded file.
traceXEnd_noX: %@ has no x or z bits at this time.
traceNoSignal: Select a signal in the waveform first.
traceNoMarker: Place the marker at the time to trace first.
traceXCondition: The condition is x or z.
traceRootTestbench: The value comes from the testbench.
traceTrustHelp_exact: Re-executing the statement gives the dumped value.
traceTrustHelp_computed: Re-executed with values the dump lacks (locals, blocking temporaries) computed.
traceTrustHelp_approximate: The result rests on assumptions listed below.
traceTrustHelp_inconsistent: Re-executing the statement does not give the dumped value.
traceError_notInDesign: This signal is not in the design model.
traceError_reloaded: The waveform was reloaded during the trace. Trace again on the reloaded file.
traceUnconfirmedHelp: Read before the reader's whole-file check of this file ran (it starts after 30 s without reads). These values are not yet confirmed by it; the badge goes when the check passes. If the check finds the file damaged, an error is shown and this result may be wrong.
traceCompiledOnly: Drivers come from the compiled design (KDB); values aren't evaluated.
traceCompiledOnly_notInSlang: Slang's design model doesn't have this instance (its module may be in a file it didn't read).
traceCompiledOnly_otherModule: Slang's design model has another module at this instance, so its statements aren't used.
traceCompiledNoWrites: The compiled design has no statement writing it here (it is driven through a port, or is an input).
traceError_notASignal: This is not a signal of its instance.
traceEngineCmux: Traced by the slang design model
traceEngineVerdi: Traced by Verdi, re-executed by the slang design model
traceBuildTitleLocal: Building the design model on this Mac
traceBuildOnce: Built once per host and extension version.
traceBuildFailedTitle: The design model could not be built on %@
traceBuildFailedTitleLocal: The design model could not be built on this Mac
traceBuildLog: Last lines of the build log:
traceVerdiStarting: Verdi is starting on the host
traceVerdiNotFound: Verdi does not know this signal
traceVerdiUnavailable_noKDB: Verdi not used: no KDB next to the FSDB (compile with vcs -kdb)
traceVerdiUnavailable_noVerdi: Verdi not used: it is not installed on the host
traceVerdiUnavailable_slowStart: Verdi not used: it did not start in time
traceVerdiUnavailable_units: Verdi not used: its time unit is not the FSDB’s (%@)
traceReason_opaque: Part of the statement is not modelled: %@
traceReason_limits: A limit was reached (an expression too large to evaluate, or more than 16 blocking temporaries on the way to the fan-in): the result may be incomplete.
traceReason_evaluator: An expression could not be evaluated: %@
traceReason_statement: A statement kind is not re-executed: %@
traceReason_delay: The block has delays; timing is approximate.
traceReason_lvalue: The assignment target is not modelled: %@
traceReason_budget: The re-execution stopped at its step limit.
traceReason_testbench: Driven by testbench code, which is not re-executed.
traceReason_force: Another instance writes this signal too (a testbench force or $deposit, or a hierarchical write), and its own drivers can't explain the value: that write is shown. It is not re-executed.
traceReason_xprop: The simulator propagated x through a condition (X-propagation).
traceReason_race: Inputs changed at the activation time; the order is assumed.
traceReason_rewrites: The block may have written this value again after %@ (too many input changes to check, or an input not in the waveform); the earlier write is assumed.
traceReason_staticLocal: Reads %@, a variable local to the block, before the block assigns it: it keeps its value from an earlier activation, which is not known here.
traceReason_targetNotDumped: The signal is not dumped; its value is computed.
traceReason_noActivation: No activation of the block was found before %@.
traceReason_notRecorded: Capture was off from %@ (a gap in the waveform file): when the value last changed there, or what it was, is not recorded.
traceReason_sinceUnknown: When the value last changed is unknown (the signal is too large for the waveform reader): a clocked step uses the last clock edge, a combinational or latch step the values at the time asked.
traceReason_initialValue: The value is the signal’s initial value.
traceReason_writeNotFound: No statement found in the design writes this signal, yet its value changed after the start or is not its initial value: a write the design model does not show made it.
traceReason_noWrite: The taken branch does not write the signal: it keeps its value.
traceReason_multiDriven: Several drivers; the one that agrees with the dump is shown.
traceReason_mismatch: Re-execution gives %2$@, not the dumped value.
traceReason_held: The latch holds the value it had at %@.
traceReason_kdbDiffers: slang’s design differs from the compiled design (KDB) here, so its statements may not be what ran: %@.
traceReason_kdbPending: The compiled design (KDB) is still loading, so this was traced with slang’s design.
traceReason_kdbNotChecked: This instance was not checked against the compiled design (KDB), so slang’s statements may not be what ran.
traceResolvedTarget: Not in the dump: its value is read via %@
traceReason_branchInferred: Branch inferred from the value change: the condition read x here, and this branch writes the value the dump shows.
traceReason_xBranch: The condition is x and the value did not change: the branch that keeps it or a branch that writes the same value may have run.
traceReason_noValueCondition: A condition reads a signal with no value (%@): no branch is assumed. The possible drivers are listed; one is named only when the dump confirms it.
traceUnconfirmedOffHelp: The reader's whole-file check is turned off (vaporview.wisp.verifyStart: off), so these values are not confirmed by it.
